info.title: 3D WebGIS Core API
info.description:
HTTP API of **3D WebGIS Core**: published layer lists, terrain / orthophoto tiles, vector GeoJSON and the chunked geodata upload used by the 3D map. Request and response bodies are JSON unless an operation says otherwise.

The dashboard's management actions (layer renaming / archiving, layer categories, users, profile) are Next.js Server Actions, not REST endpoints, and are not part of this document.

## Authentication

Every `/geodata/*` endpoint needs a signed-in user. Sessions are NextAuth v4 JWTs kept in an HTTP-only cookie: `next-auth.session-token` (`__Secure-next-auth.session-token` over HTTPS). On this page your browser sends that cookie by itself, so **Try it out** runs as you.

API clients sign in with the credentials flow and keep a cookie jar:

1. `GET /api/auth/csrf` → `{ "csrfToken": "..." }` plus a `next-auth.csrf-token` cookie.
2. `POST /api/auth/callback/credentials` as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` with `csrfToken`, `id_user` (username or email), `password`, `remember=true|false` and `json=true`. Success is `200 { "url": ... }` with the session cookie; wrong credentials are `401`.
3. Send the cookie with every request. `GET /api/auth/session` shows the signed-in user; `POST /api/auth/signout` (with a fresh `csrfToken`) clears the cookie.

```bash
curl -c jar -b jar http://localhost:3000/api/auth/csrf
curl -c jar -b jar http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/credentials \
  --data-urlencode csrfToken=<token> --data-urlencode id_user=<username> \
  --data-urlencode password=<password> -d remember=false -d json=true
curl -b jar http://localhost:3000/geodata/layers/all
```

Without "Remember me" a session ends after 120 idle minutes; with it, after 30 days. Deleting a user or changing their password revokes their sessions. Sign-in is throttled (20 attempts per minute per IP, 5 failed attempts per identifier and IP). OAuth sign-in (Discord, GitHub, Google, when configured) is a browser redirect flow and cannot be used by API clients.

## Roles

| Role | Access |
| --- | --- |
| `admin` | Everything: layer lists, tiles, vector data, uploads, recent uploads, layer deletion. |
| `engineering` | Read-only: layer lists, categories, icons, tiles and vector data. |

A request without a valid session gets `401 {"message":"Unauthenticated."}`; a role without access gets `403 {"message":"This action is unauthorized."}`.

## CSRF protection

`POST` and `DELETE` requests to `/geodata/*` must come from the app's own origin: when the request has an `Origin` header it must equal the app origin (or `APP_URL`), otherwise `Sec-Fetch-Site` must be `same-origin` or `none`. Anything else gets `419 {"message":"CSRF token mismatch."}`. Non-browser clients that send neither header pass. The NextAuth endpoints use their own `csrfToken` instead (see Authentication).

## Errors

Errors of `/geodata/*` are JSON: `{ "message": "..." }`, and for validation failures (422) `{ "message": "<first error>", "errors": { "<field>": ["..."] } }`.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | Malformed JSON body |
| 401 / 403 | Not signed in / role not allowed |
| 404 | Not found, not published, or not yours (upload sessions and jobs) |
| 409 | Conflicting state (upload incomplete or already submitted, layer still processing) |
| 410 | Upload session expired |
| 413 | Upload quota exceeded (2000 MB in flight per user) |
| 419 | CSRF check failed |
| 422 | Validation failed |
| 429 | Rate limit (`Retry-After` header) or too many active uploads |
| 500 | Unexpected error (the message is generic in production) |
| 503 | Upload could not be queued |
| 507 | Not enough free disk space |

Tile endpoints answer a missing tile with a plain-text (or empty) 404 instead of JSON.

## Upload flow

Uploads are admin-only and limited per user per minute: `upload-start` 20 (start, cancel, assemble), `upload-chunks` 240, `upload-status` 120 (session and job status).

1. **Start a session**: `POST /geodata/upload/sessions` with `{ fileName, fileSize, requestId }` → `201 { session }`. Use one random UUID `requestId` per file and reuse it on retries. Allowed extensions: `.tif`, `.tiff`, `.geotiff`, `.geojson`, `.dxf`, `.dwg`, `.str`, `.zip`; at most 1000 MB per file, 4 active sessions and 2000 MB in flight per user. Unfinished sessions expire 24 hours after the last stored chunk.
2. **Send the chunks**: split the file into `session.chunkSize` (2 MB) pieces and `POST /geodata/upload/chunk` each one as `multipart/form-data` with `file`, `identifier`, `chunkIndex` and `checksum` (lowercase hex SHA-256 of the chunk). Order does not matter and retries are safe. To resume, `GET /geodata/upload/sessions/{identifier}` and send the indexes missing from `chunks`.
3. **Assemble**: `POST /geodata/upload/assemble-raster` (DEM GeoTIFF plus an optional orthophoto session) or `POST /geodata/upload/assemble-vector` (GeoJSON, zipped Shapefile, DXF, DWG, Surpac STR) → `202 { job_id }`. The layer is created with status `processing`.
4. **Poll**: `GET /geodata/upload/status/{job_id}` until `status` is `done` (the response then contains the layer) or `failed`.

`DELETE /geodata/upload/sessions/{identifier}` cancels an upload that has not been assembled yet. Files are verified by the background worker (format signature, Shapefile archive limits), so a bad file shows up as a `failed` job rather than an HTTP error.

get.summary: Get a CSRF token for sign-in / sign-out
get.description: Step 1 of the credentials sign-in. Returns the token and sets the `next-auth.csrf-token` cookie; send both (token in the form body, cookie in `Cookie`) to `POST /api/auth/callback/credentials` or `POST /api/auth/signout`.

post.summary: Sign in with username / email and password
post.description:
Step 2 of the credentials sign-in (NextAuth credentials provider). Send the form with the cookies from `GET /api/auth/csrf`; on success the response sets the JWT session cookie (`next-auth.session-token`, `__Secure-next-auth.session-token` over HTTPS) that authenticates every other request.

Throttled: 20 attempts per minute per IP and 5 failed attempts per identifier + IP; a throttled attempt answers 401 like wrong credentials, with the wait time in the message.

Note NextAuth's quirk: a missing or mismatched `csrfToken` answers **200** with `url` ending in `/api/auth/signin?csrf=true` and no session cookie, so check for the cookie (or call `GET /api/auth/session`).

200.description: Signed in (session cookie set), or CSRF check failed (no cookie, `url` ends in `?csrf=true`).

302.description: Without `json=true`: browser-style redirect (to `callbackUrl` on success, else to the login page).

401.description: Wrong credentials or too many attempts; the message is in the `error` query parameter of `url`.

failed.summary: These credentials do not match our records.

throttled.summary: Too many login attempts. Please try again in 42 seconds.

get.description: The signed-in user, `{}` without a session, or `{ expires, invalid: true }` when the token belongs to a deleted user or predates a password change. Calling it also extends a session without "Remember me".

post.description: Clears the session cookie (`Max-Age=0`). Sessions are stateless JWTs, so a copied token stays valid until it expires unless the password is changed. A missing or wrong `csrfToken` signs nothing out and points `url` to `/api/auth/signout?csrf=true` (302 without `json=true`).

get.description:
Published terrain and vector layers for the map's layer panel, grouped by layer category (category sort order, newest layer first). Layers without a category are listed under the `other` category; categories without a matching layer are left out.

**Role:** any signed-in user (`admin`, `engineering`).

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring of the layer name (trimmed; empty = no filter).

parameters.name: month_year
parameters.description: Only layers uploaded in this month (UTC), as `YYYY-MM`. Other formats are ignored; an impossible month such as `2026-13` matches nothing.

layers.summary: One terrain and one vector layer

get.description:
Newest published terrain layers, for the comparison-terrain pickers of the Cut & Fill and Profile tools.

**Role:** any signed-in user (`admin`, `engineering`).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of layers. Clamped to 1–100; a non-numeric value counts as 1.

get.description:
The 10 newest conversion jobs (any uploader), for the Data panel.

**Role:** `admin`.

jobs.summary: A running and a finished job

delete.description:
Deletes the layer with its conversion job, logs, upload sessions and source files, then queues the removal of its tiles, files and PostGIS table. Refused (409) while the conversion is queued or processing, unless the job has been idle for more than 3 hours. Cannot be undone.

**Role:** `admin`.

value.message: Layer deleted.

409.description: The layer's conversion is still running.

value.message: This layer is still being processed. Wait until its conversion finishes or fails before deleting it.

get.description:
All layer categories in sort order (for the upload form's category picker).

**Role:** any signed-in user (`admin`, `engineering`).

Uploaded category icon referenced by `icon_url`. Only `layer-categories/<name>.png|webp` files are served.

**Role:** any signed-in user (`admin`, `engineering`).

Quantized-mesh `layer.json` of a published terrain layer: the entry point of `CesiumTerrainProvider.fromUrl(tileset_url)`. Tile URL templates get a `terrain_revision` parameter appended to bust stale browser caches.

**Role:** any signed-in user (`admin`, `engineering`).

404.description: Unknown or unpublished layer (JSON), or a published layer whose `layer.json` is missing on disk (`text/plain` "Metadata not found").

get.description:
One quantized-mesh-1.0 tile (TMS scheme, EPSG:4326) of a published terrain layer. Tiles are stored gzip-compressed and sent decompressed (the HTTP layer may re-compress them). Zoom levels follow the layer's `available` ranges (conversion range 0–15).

**Role:** any signed-in user (`admin`, `engineering`).

404.description: Unknown / unpublished layer or malformed path (JSON), or a tile outside the dataset (`text/plain` "Terrain tile not found", `Cache-Control: no-store`).

get.description:
One 256 px XYZ (Web Mercator) PNG tile of a published terrain layer's orthophoto, as templated by `terrain_detail.ortho_tiles_url`. Available zooms: `ortho_min_zoom`–`ortho_max_zoom`.

**Role:** any signed-in user (`admin`, `engineering`).

404.description: Unknown / unpublished layer or malformed path (JSON), or a tile outside the orthophoto (empty body).

get.description:
Streams every feature of a published vector layer (its PostGIS table) as one GeoJSON FeatureCollection in WGS84. Large layers produce large responses; the body is streamed, so read it incrementally. A published layer without a vector table (e.g. a terrain layer) returns an empty collection.

**Role:** any signed-in user (`admin`, `engineering`).

400.description: The layer's table name failed the safety check (corrupt layer metadata).

value.message: Invalid table name pattern.

post.description:
Step 1 of the upload. Creates a session for one file, to be sent in 2 MB chunks. With a `requestId` the call is idempotent: repeating it returns the existing session (still 201), so a client that lost the response can retry safely.

Quotas per user: at most 4 active sessions (uploading or queued) and 2000 MB in flight; the server also keeps 512 MB of disk free after reserving twice the file size.

Rate limit `upload-start`: 20/min. **Role:** `admin`.

post.description:
Step 2 of the upload. Send each chunk (`chunkSize` = 2 MB, the last one holds the remainder) with its SHA-256. Chunks may arrive in any order and in parallel; re-sending a stored chunk with the same checksum is a no-op, a different one is a 409. Each stored chunk extends the session's expiry.

Rate limit `upload-chunks`: 240/min. **Role:** `admin`.

post.summary: Submit a terrain upload (DEM + optional orthophoto)
post.description:
Step 3 for terrain: submits a completed DEM GeoTIFF session (and optionally an orthophoto GeoTIFF session). The worker assembles and verifies the files, then builds quantized-mesh terrain tiles and XYZ orthophoto tiles.

Creates the layer (status `processing`) and a queued conversion job, and answers 202 with the job id to poll (step 4). Idempotent: repeating the request with the same parameters returns the same `job_id`; different parameters for an already submitted session are a 409. Verification failures (file signature, archive limits: 1000 entries, 2000 MB uncompressed, ratio 100:1) surface later as a `failed` job.

Rate limit `upload-start`: 20/min. **Role:** `admin`.

chunkSize.description: Bytes per chunk (2 MB); the last chunk holds the remainder.

job_id.description: Conversion job id once the upload was submitted.

expiresAt.description: When an unfinished session expires (24 h after creation or the last stored chunk).

fileName.description: Original file name (at most 255 bytes, no control characters or `<>:"/\|?*`). Allowed extensions: `.tif`, `.tiff`, `.geotiff`, `.geojson`, `.dxf`, `.dwg`, `.str`, `.zip`.

fileSize.description: File size in bytes, at most 1000 MB (GEODATA_MAX_UPLOAD_MB).

requestId.description: Client-generated idempotency key for this file. Repeating a request with the same `requestId` returns the existing session (409 if the file name or size differ). Omit it to always create a new session.

file.description: The chunk bytes: exactly `min(chunkSize, fileSize - chunkIndex * chunkSize)` bytes, at most 2048 KB.

checksum.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the chunk bytes.

sourceEpsg.description: Source coordinate reference system as `EPSG:<code>`. Required for CAD / Surpac files (`.dxf`, `.dwg`, `.str`); GeoTIFF, GeoJSON and Shapefile uploads carry their own CRS.
